scope.purpose: Show one of several panels of related content in the same place, with a list of tabs to switch between them.
useCases: Views of a record (overview, activity, files).
A vertical list of sections beside their content.
exclusions: Navigation between pages (links styled as tabs).
Overflow menu or scroll buttons for many tabs (the list scrolls).
alternatives: SegmentedControl or RadioGroup for a choice of value.
Accordion to show several sections at once.

fixtures: Phosphor glyphs re-exported by examples/icon/glyphs.ts for the leading icon example.

decisionsTaken: One appearance (line): the selected tab has a 2 px bar (border.width.strong) in color.item.indicator over a 1 px color.border.subtle line, on the edge facing the panels (block end horizontally, inline end vertically).
Unselected labels in color.content.secondary, selected and hovered labels in color.content.primary (color.item.*.content); hover paints color.item.hover.surface behind the tab with radius.control.
Tabs follow size (size.control.{size}, typography.label.{size}, padding and gap of controls) like Button.
Roving focus shared with Toolbar in a new copyable module lib/roving-focus (shared-code decision of 2026-10-31): arrows wrap, Home and End, right-to-left reversal, disabled items skipped.
Disabled tabs and toolbar items are skipped by the arrow keys (the WAI-ARIA patterns allow both); Menu keeps reaching disabled items, since its items are discovered by browsing a popup list.
activation automatic by default (WAI-ARIA recommendation when panels show at once), manual available for slow panels.
A horizontal list that overflows scrolls inline and keeps the focused and selected tab visible; no scroll buttons in v1.
Trigger trailing slot accepts a Counter or a Badge, sized by the tab.

Svelte API: a `list` snippet holds the TabsTrigger children and `children` the TabsPanel children; triggers register in source order so that the fallback to the first enabled tab also works during server rendering (a value not registered yet is trusted until mount).

Round 2 (user: "attention à ne pas réinventer la roue"): Tabs now uses Bits UI Tabs (roles, ids, roving focus with right-to-left and disabled tabs, activation modes); ggbrick adds the fallback to the first enabled tab and renders the selection through the child snippets so that server rendering selects a tab (Bits UI reads the value before the triggers register). The roving-focus module moved into the Toolbar folder (its only user).

Bits UI decision for wave 4 reviewed: Tabs and Accordion use it; Select and Combobox keep the own primitive (Bits UI content positions with floating-ui and its own dismissal layers, against the native top layer); Pagination keeps its own algorithm (Bits UI shows 6 then 7 items, the contract asks a constant count) and its link mode; Toolbar keeps its roving focus (Bits UI Toolbar needs every item wrapped in Toolbar.Button).

Round 3: appearance contained (default, the user's reference: tabs as buttons in a container, the selected one raised) and line (the first design). In a horizontal contained list the tabs share the inline size equally, never below their content. In dark the raised tab is darker than the muted container (token values); to judge at the gate.

Wave 4 Figma parity gate (user, 2026-11-12): the Figma Tabs is the tab list only (the panels stay in the contract and the code, which link them to the tabs); the selected tab of a line list paints its label in the indicator color (option C, role selectedColor), and hover is painted behind unselected tabs only in both appearances.
nextAction: Documentation (skill ggb-docs): the maintained page, the docs-site check, the site preview for the review; then the final consistency pass and the pull request of the wave.
implementationNotes: Panels stay mounted and are hidden with the hidden attribute (form state is kept).
A panel without focusable content is a tab stop (tabindex 0), checked by a MutationObserver.
A Counter or Badge in the trailing slot takes the size the application gives it (as in Button).
